metadata.title: Dirac cohomology, the projective supermodules of the symmetric group and the Vogan morphism

nodes.name: Real root system
nodes.statement: We fix a real root system $\{V, \Phi, V^\vee, \Phi^\vee\}$, where $\Phi$ is the set of roots inside the real vector space $ V$, we have a perfect bilinear pairing $B( \ , \ ) : V \times V^\vee \to \mathbb{R}$ The roots are in bijections with the coroots such that $B( \alpha , \alpha^\vee ) = 2$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a real root system with roots, coroots and a perfect pairing B with B(alpha, alpha^vee)=2.

nodes.name: Reflections s_alpha
nodes.statement: We define reflections $$s_\alpha : V \to V, \hspace{0.75cm} s_\alpha (v) = v - B( v, \alpha^\vee )\alpha.$$

nodes.name: Weyl group W
nodes.statement: Let $W$ be the subgroup of $GL(V)$ generated by the reflections $s_\alpha$ for all $\alpha \in \Phi$.
differentia: generated by the reflections $s_\alpha$ for all $\alpha \in \Phi$

nodes.name: Invariant form, positive and simple roots
nodes.statement: Fix a $W$-invariant bilinear form on $V$, $( \ , \ )$ on $V$, a set of positive (resp. simple) roots $\Phi^+$ (resp. $\Pi$).

nodes.name: Extended Weyl group W_#
nodes.statement: We let $\delta$ denote the automorphism $W$ given by the conjugation by $w_0$ on $V$, where $w_0$ is the longest element in $W$. Then let $W_\#$ be the extension of $W$ by $\delta$. Explicitly $$W_\# = \langle W , \delta : \delta^2 = 1, \delta w \delta = \delta(w) \text{ for all } w \in W \rangle.$$
nodes.statement_short: W_# is W extended by the automorphism delta = conjugation by the longest element w_0.

nodes.name: Root datum of the symmetric group S_n
nodes.statement: Let $W$ be the symmetric group $S_n$. The underlying root space is $V = \mathrm{span}_{\mathbb{C}} \{\xi_1,\ldots ,\xi_n\}$ and we will fix the simple roots $\Pi = \{\alpha_i =\xi_i-\xi_{i+1} : i = 1,..,n-1\},$ and positive roots $\Phi^+ = \{\xi_i-\xi_j : i <j \}$. The bilinear form is $( \xi_i , \xi_j ) = \delta_{ij}$. We have the presentation; $$S_n = \langle s_1,\ldots ,s_{n-1} : (s_is_j)^{m(i,j)} = 1 \rangle.$$ Here $m(i,i) = 1$ and $m(i,j) = -( \alpha_i , \alpha_j )( \alpha_j , \alpha_i ) +2$ if $i\neq j$ \cite{M74}. The automorphism $\delta$ come from the action of $-w_0$ on $\Phi$ hence $\delta(\alpha_i) = \alpha_{n-i}$, and $\delta(s_\alpha) = s_{\delta(\alpha)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Root system, Coxeter presentation and the automorphism delta for W = S_n.

nodes.name: Graded Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: The graded Hecke algebra $\mathbb{H}$ associated to a Weyl group $W$, $V$ and $( \ ,\ )$ is the associative unital $\mathbb{C}$-algebra generated by $\{ \xi \in V\}$ and $\{w\in W\}$ such that there exist injections, induced by the inclusion of generators, $$S(V) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{H},$$ $$\mathbb{C}[W] \hookrightarrow \mathbb{H}.$$ Furthermore, for every simple root $\alpha \in \Pi$, there exist cross-relations, $$\xi \cdot s_\alpha - s_\alpha \cdot s_\alpha(\xi) = ( \alpha , \xi ).$$
nodes.statement_short: Graded Hecke algebra: generated by S(V) and C[W] with cross relations xi s_alpha - s_alpha s_alpha(xi) = (alpha, xi).

nodes.name: Extended graded Hecke algebra H_#
nodes.statement: We define $\mathbb{H}_\#$ to be an extension of the graded Hecke algebra by $\delta$. Explicitly, $$ \mathbb{H}_\# = \langle \mathbb{H} , \delta \rangle = \langle \mathbb{H}, \delta : \delta^2 = 1, \delta h \delta = \delta(h) \text{ for all } h \in \mathbb{H} \rangle. $$

nodes.name: Clifford algebra
nodes.statement: The Clifford algebra $C(V)$ defined by $V$ and the symmetric bilinear form $( \ , \ )$ on $V$ is the associative unital algebra generated by elements in $V$ such that $$\xi\xi' + \xi'\xi = 2( \xi' , \xi ) \text{ for all } \xi, \xi' \in V.$$
nodes.label: Clifford

nodes.name: Clifford algebra C(n) for S_n
nodes.statement: For $S_n$, the vector space $V$ has the euclidean norm and is of dimension $n$. In this case we will denote the Clifford algebra for the rank $n$ case by $C(n)$.

nodes.name: Filtration of the Clifford algebra
nodes.statement: The Clifford algebra has a natural filtration by $\mathbb{Z}$. Each generator is given degree one and then $C(V)_n$ is the span of all elements of $C(V)$ with degree $n$ or lower.

nodes.name: Z/2Z grading of the Clifford algebra
nodes.statement: $C(V)$ also has a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ grading, $$C(V) = C(V)_{\mathrm{even}}\oplus C(V)_{\mathrm{odd}}$$ where $C(V)_{\mathrm{even}}$ is the span of all homogeneous elements of even degree and likewise for $C(V)_{\mathrm{odd}}$.

nodes.name: Transpose and parity involution on C(V)
nodes.statement: Define the transpose of $C(V)$ be the antiautomorphism defined by $\xi^t = -\xi$ for all elements of $V$ and let $\epsilon: C(V) \to C(V)$ to the involution which is the identity on $C(V)_{\mathrm{even}}$ and acts as $-1$ on $C(V)_{\mathrm{odd}}$.

nodes.name: Pin group
nodes.statement: The Pin group is $$Pin(V) = \{g\in C(V)^\times | g^t = g^{-1} \text{ and } \epsilon(g) \xi g^{-1} \in V, \text{ for all } \xi \in V\}.$$

nodes.name: Projection p: Pin(V) -> O(V)
nodes.statement: This group is a double cover of the orthogonal group on $V$ with projection $p: Pin(V) \to O(V)$, $$p(g)(\xi) = \epsilon(g)\xi g^{-1}.$$

nodes.name: Double cover W~ of W
nodes.statement: Let $\tilde{W}$ be the preimage of $W$ via $p$, $$\tilde{W} = p^{-1} (W).$$

nodes.name: Morris presentation of the double cover
nodes.statement: \cite[3.2]{M74} The double cover $\tilde{W}$ of $W$ admits a presentation akin to Coxeter presentations for a Weyl group, $$\tilde{W} = \langle z , \tilde{s}_\alpha \text{ for all } \alpha \in \Pi : z^2 = 1, (\tilde{s}_\alpha \tilde{s}_\beta) ^{m(\alpha,\beta)} = z^{m(\alpha,\beta)-1}, z \text{ is central } \rangle$$ where $m(\alpha, \alpha) =1$ and $m(\alpha,\beta) = \langle \alpha , \beta \rangle \langle \beta , \alpha \rangle+ 2$.
conclusions: The double cover $\tilde{W}$ of $W$ admits a presentation akin to Coxeter presentations for a Weyl group
nodes.statement_short: The double cover W~ has a Coxeter-like presentation with central z, z^2=1 and twisted braid relations.
nodes.label: morris

nodes.name: Morris presentation by positive roots
nodes.statement: Morris also showed that one can define a presentation of $W$ with generators for each positive root \cite[3.2]{M74}, $$W = \langle z , \tilde{s}_\alpha \text{ for all } \alpha \in \Phi^+ : \tilde{s}_\alpha^2 = 1, \tilde{s}_\alpha \tilde{s}_\beta \tilde{s}_\beta = z \tilde{s}_\gamma, \gamma = s_\alpha(\beta), z^2 =1, z \text{ is central}\rangle.$$
nodes.statement_short: Presentation of the cover with one generator per positive root.

nodes.name: Double cover W~_#
nodes.statement: Hence we can also define $\tilde{W}_\# = p^{-1}(W_\#)$.

nodes.name: Element omega
nodes.statement: The non scalar element in the preimage of $-1$ is $\omega$ which can be formulated in terms of an orthonormal basis $\{\xi_1,\ldots ,\xi_n\}$ of $V$, as $$\omega = \xi_1\xi_2\ldots \xi_n \in Pin(V).$$

nodes.name: Groups W~' and W~_#'
nodes.statement: We will also define $\tilde{W}'$ and $\tilde{W}_\#'$ to be $$\tilde{W}' = \begin{cases} \tilde{W} \cap C(V)_{\mathrm{even}}, & \dim V \text{ even }, \\ \tilde{W}, & \dim V \text{ odd }, \end{cases}$$ and $$\tilde{W}_\#' = \begin{cases} \langle \tilde{W} \cap C(V)_{\mathrm{even}}, \omega \rangle, & \dim V even, \\ \tilde{W}_\#, & \dim V odd. \end{cases}$$
nodes.statement_short: W~' and W~_#' restrict to the even part of the Clifford algebra when dim V is even.

nodes.name: Twisted group algebra T_n
nodes.statement: \cite[p. 303]{S82} Let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be the twisted group algebra of $S_n$ over $\mathbb{C}$. Explicitly $\mathcal{T}_n$ is the unital associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra generated by $\tau_i$ for $i = 1 \ldots n-1$ such that $$\tau_i^2 = 1, (\tau_i \tau_j)^{m(i,j)} = (-1)^{m(i,j)-1}.$$

nodes.name: Pseudo-transpositions tau_alpha
nodes.statement: Following the presentation from Theorem \ref{morris} we could label the generators with the simple roots, $\alpha \in \Pi$. Then $\mathcal{T}_n$ becomes $$\langle \tau_{\alpha}, \alpha \in \Pi : (\tau_\alpha\tau_\beta)^{m(\alpha,\beta)} = (-1)^{m(\alpha,\beta) -1} \rangle.$$ Finally we also have $$\mathcal{T}_n = \langle \tau_\alpha \text{ for all } \alpha \in \Phi^+ : \tau_\alpha^2 = 1, \tau_\alpha \tau_\beta \tau_\beta = - \tau_\gamma, \gamma = s_\alpha(\beta)\rangle.$$ So by the above presentation, similarly to the symmetric group, one has for each positive root, $\alpha \in \Phi^+$, a \ `pseudo-transposition' $\tau_\alpha$. Note that this $\tau_\alpha$ is equal to the the `transposition' $[ij]$ defined in \cite[3.1]{BK01}. We will switch between labelings of the generators whenever it clarifies explanation.
nodes.statement_short: Presentations of T_n by simple and by positive roots, giving a pseudo-transposition tau_alpha per positive root.

nodes.name: Genuine projective irreducible representations
nodes.statement: The genuine projective irreducible representations of $\tilde{S}_n$ are the irreducible representations that do not descend to a representation of $S_n$.

nodes.name: Decomposition of the group algebra of the double cover
nodes.statement: The group algebra for $\tilde{S}_n$ decomposes as $$\mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n] \cong \mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n]/(z -1) \oplus \mathbb{C}[\tilde{S}_n ]/(z+1) \cong \mathbb{C}[S_n] \oplus \mathcal{T}_n.$$
conclusions: The group algebra for $\tilde{S}_n$ decomposes as

nodes.name: Vector superspace and superalgebra
nodes.statement: A vector superspace is a vector space $U$ which is $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-graded, $U = U_0 \oplus U_1$. Similarly, a superalgebra is an algebra which is $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-graded.

nodes.name: Super endomorphism algebra End(U)
nodes.statement: For a vector superspace $U$ we can define $\mathrm{End}(U)$ to be isomorphic to $\mathrm{End}(U_0 \oplus U_1)$ as an ungraded algebra then as a superalgebra the even elements fix $U_i$ and odd elements take $U_0$ to $U_1$ and $U_1$ to $U_0$.

nodes.name: Supermodule
nodes.statement: A supermodule of a superalgebra $A$ is a super vector space $U$ along with a graded map from $A \to End(U)$.
differentia: along with a graded map from $A \to End(U)$

nodes.name: Supermodules of type M and type Q
nodes.statement: Let $U$ be an $A$-supermodule. Then $U$ is of type M if, when one forgets the grading, $U$ is an irreducible $A$ ungraded module. The module $U$ is of type Q if it is reducible as an $A$ ungraded module.

nodes.name: Irreducible supermodules after forgetting the grading
nodes.statement: When one forgets the grading all irreducible supermodules are either still irreducible or decompose into two irreducible parts.

nodes.name: Clifford algebra is supersimple
nodes.statement: However when we consider supermodules, $C(V)$ is supersimple; it always has exactly one simple supermodule, $\mathcal{S}$ \cite[12.2.4]{K05}. When $\dim(V)$ is odd then $\mathcal{S}$ is of type Q and when $\dim(V)$ is even the supermodule is of type M.
conclusions: $C(V)$ is supersimple; it always has exactly one simple supermodule, $\mathcal{S}$
nodes.statement_short: C(V) has a unique simple supermodule S, of type Q for dim V odd and type M for dim V even.

nodes.name: Supertrace
nodes.statement: The supertrace on the representation $U= U_0 \oplus U_1$ is defined to be zero on odd elements and, on even elements, $$\mathrm{str}_V(a) = \mathrm{tr}_0 (a) - \mathrm{tr}_1(a)$$ where $tr_i(a)$ is the trace of the matrix corresponding to $a$ restricted to $U_i$.

nodes.name: Partition
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda = (\lambda_1,..,\lambda_r) \in \mathbb{N}^r$. The set $\lambda$ is a partition of $n$ if $\sum_{i=1}^r \lambda_i = n$ and $\lambda_1\geq \lambda_2 \geq \ldots \geq \lambda_r$.

nodes.name: Set of partitions P(n)
nodes.statement: We will denote the set of partitions of $n$ by $\mathcal{P}(n)$.

nodes.name: Length of a partition and strict partition
nodes.statement: We define the length of a partition, $l(\lambda)$, to be $\#\{\lambda_i : \lambda_i > 0\}$ We say a partition $\lambda \vdash n$ is strict if $\lambda_1>\lambda_2>\ldots >\lambda_r$.

nodes.name: Young diagram
nodes.statement: For a partition $\lambda \vdash n$ we associate to it a set of boxes forming the Young diagram. For $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\ldots ,\lambda_r)$, we define the Young diagram to be $$\lambda = \{ (i,j) : 1 < i < l(\lambda) \text{ and } 1< j < \lambda_i \}.$$

nodes.name: Shifted partitions
nodes.statement: The set of shifted partitions of $n$ is the same as the set of strict partitions of $n$. However, we will consider a different $Young$ diagram for a shifted partition than the associated Young diagram of a normal partition. We will write $\lambda \vDash n$ to denote a shifted partition of $n$ and $\mathcal{SP}(n)$ is the set of shifted partitions of $n$.

nodes.name: Shifted Young diagram
nodes.statement: Given a shifted partition $\lambda = (\lambda_1,\ldots ,\lambda_r) \vDash n$ we associate a shifted Young diagram, $$\lambda = \{ (i,j) : 1 < i < l(\lambda) \text{ and } i< j < i+ \lambda_i -1 \}.$$

nodes.name: Young tableau
nodes.statement: A Young tableau of shape $\lambda$ is a numbering of $1$ to $n$ of the Young diagram associated to $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Notation [lambda]
nodes.statement: We will write $[\lambda]$ for a Young tableau of shape $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Notation [[lambda]] for shifted tableaux
nodes.statement: Similarly $[[\lambda]]$ will denote a numbering of the shifted Young diagram associated to $\lambda \vDash n$.

nodes.name: Standard (shifted) Young tableau
nodes.statement: A standard Young tableau (resp. shifted) is a Young tableau (resp. shifted) such that along each row and column the numbers increase.

nodes.name: Conjugate partition
nodes.statement: Given a partition $\lambda$ we write $\lambda'$ for its conjugate partition, which is the reflection of the Young diagram in its main diagonal.

nodes.name: Conjugate of (3,1)
nodes.statement: If $\lambda = (3,1)$ then $\lambda' = (2,1,1)$, $$\lambda = \yng(3,1), \lambda' = \yng(2,1,1).$$

nodes.name: Diagonal embedding rho
nodes.statement: Let $\rho$ be the diagonal embedding of $\tilde{W}_\#$ into $\mathbb{H}_\#\otimes C(V)$; $$\rho (w) = p(w) \otimes w, \text{ for all } w \in \tilde{W}_\#.$$

nodes.name: Anti-automorphism * and xi~
nodes.statement: Let $*$ be the linear anti-automorphism on $\mathbb{H}$ defined by $$w^* = w^{-1}, \xi^* = w_0 \delta(\xi)w_0, \text{ for all } w\in W \text{ and } \xi \in V.$$ We can extend $*$ to $\mathbb{H}_\#$ by defining it to fix $\delta$. Given $\xi$, let $$\tilde{\xi} = \frac{1}{2}(\xi - \xi^*).$$

nodes.name: Dirac element
nodes.statement: Let $\{\xi_1,\ldots ,\xi_n\}$ be an orthonormal basis of $V$. The Dirac element $\mathcal{D}$ in $\mathbb{H}_\#\otimes C(V)$ is defined to be, $$\mathcal{D} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \tilde{\xi}_i \otimes \xi_i.$$

nodes.name: Dirac operator D
nodes.statement: For any $\mathbb{H}_\#$-module $X$ and $C(V)$-module $\mathcal{S}$ the Dirac element $\mathcal{D}$ defines an operator $D: X\otimes \mathcal{S} \to X\otimes \mathcal{S}$.

nodes.name: Odd and even parts D^+- of the Dirac operator
nodes.statement: Furthermore, since $\mathcal{D}$ is odd, the operator $D$ interchanges the even and odd spaces of $X\otimes \mathcal{S}$, $$D^\pm : X\otimes \mathcal{S}^\pm \to X\otimes \mathcal{S}^\mp.$$

nodes.name: Extended Dirac cohomology
nodes.statement: The extended Dirac cohomology of $X$ (with respect to $\mathcal{S}$) is $$H^D_\#(X) = \ker(D_\#) / \ker(D_\#)\cap \mathrm{im}(D_\#).$$

nodes.name: Extended Dirac cohomology H^{D+-}
nodes.statement: Let, $$H^{D^\pm}_\#(X) = \ker(D^\pm_\#) / \ker(D^\pm_\#)\cap \mathrm{im}(D^\mp_\#).$$

nodes.name: Extended Dirac index
nodes.statement: The extended Dirac index is $$I_\#(X) = H^{D^+}_\#(X) - H^{D^-}_\#(X)$$ defined as a virtual $\tilde{W}_\#'$-module.

nodes.name: Dirac index as a tensor product
nodes.statement: \cite[5.10]{CH15} Let $X$ be an $\mathbb{H}_\#$-module. The Dirac index can be expressed as a tensor, $I_\#(X) = X \otimes (\mathcal{S}^+ - \mathcal{S}^-).$ Hence it is exact. Furthermore for $w \in \tilde{W}'$, $$ tr(w, I_\#(X)) = tr(p(w),X)tr(w,S^+ - S^-).$$
assumptions: Let $X$ be an $\mathbb{H}_\#$-module.
nodes.statement_short: The extended Dirac index equals X tensor (S+ - S-), so it is exact, with the corresponding trace formula.
nodes.label: CH15prop5.10

nodes.name: Extended Dirac index for supermodules
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $\mathbb{H}_\#$-supermodule, concentrated in degree zero, and $\mathcal{S}$ be a $C(V)$-supermodule.Then $I_\#(X)$ is a $\tilde{W}_\#$-supermodule and in the Grothendieck group, $$I_\#(X) = X \otimes \mathcal{S}.$$
assumptions: Let $X$ be an $\mathbb{H}_\#$-supermodule, concentrated in degree zero, and $\mathcal{S}$ be a $C(V)$-supermodule.
nodes.statement_short: For supermodules the extended Dirac index is X tensor S in the Grothendieck group, with no need to restrict W~_#.
nodes.label: superdirac

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.5
nodes.statement: From Theorem \ref{CH15prop5.10} we can describe the trace of $w \in \tilde{W}$ on $I_\#(X)$ as a product of the trace on $X$ and the difference of the trace on $\mathcal{S}^+$ and $\mathcal{S}^-$. However this is just the product of the supertrace of the modules $X$ and $\mathcal{S}$; $$ \mathrm{tr}(w, I_\#(X)) = \mathrm{tr}(p(w),X)\mathrm{tr}(w,S^+ - S^-) = \mathrm{str}(p(w),X)\mathrm{str}(w,S).$$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the trace formula of Proposition 3.4 as a product of supertraces.

nodes.name: Semisimple Lie algebra g
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra with Weyl group $W$.

nodes.name: Springer fibre B_e
nodes.statement: Then, for an element $e$ in the nilpotent cone $\mathcal{N}$, we let $\mathcal{B}_e$ denote the variety of Borel subalgebras of $\mathfrak{g}$ containing $e$.

nodes.name: q-graded module X_q(e)
nodes.statement: Let $e$ be an element in the nilpotent cone $\mathcal{N} \subset \mathfrak{g}$, $\mathcal{B}_e$ the variety of Borel subalgebras containing $e$ and $d_e$ be the dimension of $\mathcal{B}_e$. The sign character of $W$ will be denoted by $\mathrm{sgn}$. Let $\textbf{q}$ be a formal symbol. Springer \cite{S78} constructed an action of $W$ on $H^j(\mathcal{B}_e)$. Define the $\textbf{q}$-graded $W$-module. $$X_{\textbf{q}}(e) = \sum_{i \geq 0} \textbf{q}^{d_e - i} H^{2i}(\mathcal{B}_e) \otimes \mathrm{sgn}.$$
nodes.statement_short: The q-graded W-module built from Springer's action on the cohomology of B_e, twisted by sgn.

nodes.name: Classification of X_q(e) by nilpotent orbits
nodes.statement: \cite[2.2]{CG97}Two $\textbf{q}$-graded $S_n$-modules $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$ and $X_{\textbf{q}}(e')$ are isomorphic if and only if $e$ is in the same conjugacy class as $e'$. Hence the isomorphism classes of $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$ can labelled by nilpotent orbits, these are equivalent to partitions of $n$. We write the isomorphism class of $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$ as $X_{\textbf{q}}(\lambda)$ where $e$ has Jordan form corresponding to a partition $\lambda$.
equivalent_conditions: $e$ is in the same conjugacy class as $e'$
conclusions: Two $\textbf{q}$-graded $S_n$-modules $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$ and $X_{\textbf{q}}(e')$ are isomorphic if and only if $e$ is in the same conjugacy class as $e'$.

nodes.name: Specialisation X_{-1}(e)
nodes.statement: We can specialise $X_{\textbf{q}}(e)$ to a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-graded module as $$X_{-1}(e)= \sum_{i \geq 0} (-1)^{d_e - i} H^{2i}(\mathcal{B}_e) \otimes \mathrm{sgn}.$$

nodes.name: Construction of tau~_lambda
nodes.statement: \cite[A.3]{CH15} For every strict partition $\lambda$ of $n$, let $\mathcal{S}$ be an ungraded spinor module and $X_{-1}(\lambda)$ be the graded module of $S_n$ corresponding to $\lambda$. Define the $\tilde{S}_n$-module, $$\tilde{\tau}_\lambda = \frac{1}{a_\lambda} X_{-1}(\lambda) \otimes S,$$ where $$a_\lambda = \begin{cases} 2^{\frac{l(\lambda)}{2}} & n \text{ even and } l(\lambda) \text{ even}, \\ 2^{\frac{l(\lambda)-1}{2}} & l(\lambda) \text{ odd}, \\ 2^{\frac{l(\lambda)-2}{2}} & n \text{ odd and } l(\lambda) \text{ even}. \end{cases}$$ If $n-l(\lambda)$ is even then $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda$ is an irreducible $\mathrm{sgn}$ self-dual $\tilde{S}_n$-module. If $n-l(\lambda)$ is odd then $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda = \tilde{\tau}^+_\lambda + \tilde{\tau}^-_\lambda$, with $\tilde{\tau}^\pm_\lambda$ irreducible modules which are $\mathrm{sgn}$ dual to each other.
assumptions: For every strict partition $\lambda$ of $n$
conclusions: If $n-l(\lambda)$ is even then $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda$ is an irreducible $\mathrm{sgn}$ self-dual $\tilde{S}_n$-module.
nodes.statement_short: tau~_lambda = X_{-1}(lambda) tensor S / a_lambda is irreducible (or splits in two sgn-dual pieces) depending on the parity of n - l(lambda).
nodes.label: alambda

nodes.name: tau~_lambda is an irreducible supermodule
nodes.statement: For a strict partition $\lambda$, when one lets $\mathcal{S}$ be a super simple spinor module, $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda$ is always an irreducible $\tilde{S}_n$-supermodule. If $n-l(\lambda)$ is even then $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda$ is type M and if $n-l(\lambda)$ is odd then $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda$ if of type Q.
assumptions: For a strict partition $\lambda$, when one lets $\mathcal{S}$ be a super simple spinor module

nodes.name: Index of X_{-1}(lambda) nonzero iff lambda strict
nodes.statement: The extended Dirac index of $X_{-1}(\lambda)$, $I_\#(X_{-1}(\lambda))$, is non-zero if and only if $\lambda$ is strict. This follows from \cite[6.1]{CH15} and the fact that nilpotent elements that are $\delta$ quasi-distinguished have Jordan form associated to a strict partition.
nodes.statement_short: I_#(X_{-1}(lambda)) is nonzero iff lambda is strict, by [CH15, 6.1] and delta quasi-distinguished nilpotents.
nodes.label: indexkilled

nodes.name: Convention tau~_lambda = 0 for non-strict lambda
nodes.statement: For ease of explanation later on in this paper, and motivated by Remark \ref{indexkilled}, we will set $\tilde{\tau}_\lambda = 0$ if $\lambda$ is not a strict partition.

nodes.name: Casimir element of H
nodes.statement: The Casimir element for $\mathbb{H}$ is $$\Omega_\mathbb{H} = \sum_{i=1}^n \xi_i^2,$$ where $\{\xi_i\}$ is an orthonormal basis for $V$.

nodes.name: Casimir of H is central
nodes.statement: The element $\Omega_{\mathbb{H}}$ is independent of the choice of orthonormal basis, it is central in $\mathbb{H}$ \cite[2.4]{BCT12}.

nodes.name: Casimir of H acts by (nu, nu)
nodes.statement:
Furthermore, let $(\pi,X)$ be an irreducible $\mathbb{H}$-module. It has an associated central character $\chi_
u$ which can be defined in terms of $
u \in \mathbb{H}$. It is shown in \cite[2.5]{BCT12} that $$\pi(\Omega_{\mathbb{H}})= ( 
u ,
